text: Seem always ignorant (unless to one's most intimate friend) of all matters of private scandal and defamation, though you should hear them a thousand times; for the parties affected always look upon the receiver to be almost as bad as the thief: and, whenever they become the topic of conversation seem to be a skeptic, though you are really a serious believer; and always take the extenuating part.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CLXXXVI, to his son, London, January 15, 1753
